newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks close lower on renewed scandal probe.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks close lower on renewed scandal probe.

text.p: Stocks closed lower on Monday on fears of economic fallout from a renewed probe into a loans scandal surrounding Hanbo Steel Co, brokers said.
The composite index ended 5.87 points, or 0.94 percent, lower at a provisional 617.26.
The central bank said shortly before the market ended that it would supply $1 billion to banks this month to help ease a dollar shortage but the move had little impact on share prices.
Analyst Koh Kyung-bae at Hyundai Securities said the prosecution probe into the Hanbo scandal would dictate the market trend in the short term.
"The prosecution probe is and will be the main factor affecting the market for the time being," Koh said.
At the weekend, state prosecutors reopened the probe into the loans-for-kickbacks scandal involving Hanbo, which was declared insolvent in January under huge debts.
The market was also hit in the morning by a news report that the government would go ahead with a plan to list state-run Korea Telecom in the fist half of this year.
But a senior finance ministry official said later the ministry would not press ahead with the listing plan unless market conditions improved.

"Banks and some blue chips attracted bargain hunters, but it is hard to see a turnaround in the overall sentiment until economic fundamentals improved," said Park Byung-moon, research manager at LG Securities.
The banking sub-index rose 4.33 percent to 320.87. Korea First Bank rose 230 won to its daily limit of 3,110 while Cho Hung Bank gained 270 won to 4,250.
Blue chips Samsung Electronics Co and Pohang Iron and Steel Co added 1,500 won and 800 won, respectively, to end at 56,700 and 44,600.
